newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco sees worker demands hurting firm's returns.
newsitem.headline: Meralco sees worker demands hurting firm's returns.

text.p: The Manila Electric Co (Meralco), the Philippines' biggest power distributor, said it will ask the Supreme Court to review a new collective bargaining agreement with its employees.
The firm said the agreement may lead to lower returns for the company and an increase in power rates.

"The entire agreement will amount to two billion pesos (over two years) and this will mean that our return-on-rate base will go down and may even reach below the mandated eight percent," Meralco spokesperson Elpi Cuna said.
Cuna said Meralco may not be able to fulfil its aim of not raising its distribution charges until 2000 if the agreement is pushed through.

The Department of Labour and Employment (DOLE) approved a collective bargaining agreement for the Meralco Employees Workers' Association (Mewa) which will mean a 4,400 peso monthly pay rise spread over a two-year period for each the union's 4,000 members. The Meralco management and Mewa earlier sought the DOLE's intervention when a deadlock was reached on the agreement.

"We hope to submit our petition to the Supreme Court by Thursday or Friday. If the collective bargaining agreement pushes through, it's going to be a bad signal for the entire business community," said Cuna.
Mewa president Numeriano Villalobos said that the union will file notice of a strike within the week citing unfair labour practices if the company appeals against the aggreement.
He said that the agreement will only amount to extra wage bills of 775 million pesos over two years and not two billion pesos.
